news.title: Gianni Infantino: Wales withdraws support for FIFA president's re-election
news.lede: Wales has become the first football association to officially withdraw support for Gianni Infantino's re-election as FIFA president. It follows the loss of confidence in Infantino's leadership after the botched attempt to sell off stakes in the World Cup. The Football Association of Wales told Sky News it "hereby confirms its withdrawal of support for the candidature of Mr Gianni Infantino, for re-election as FIFA president for the 2027-2031 term".

news.title: Wales first nation to withdraw support for Infantino
news.lede: Gianni Infantino rose to prominence via a number of roles at Uefa. Wales have become the first nation to publicly withdraw backing for Gianni Infantino's bid to continue his leadership of Fifa. It follows the loss of confidence in the Fifa president following his scrapped plans to sell stakes in its competitions to private investment firms. The Football Association of Wales (FAW) has confirmed "its withdrawal of support for the candidature of Mr Gianni Infantino for re-election as Fifa president for the 2027-2031 term".

news.title: Sports - Infantino under growing pressure after FIFA scraps World Cup investor proposal
news.lede: FIFA President Gianni Infantino is under pressure after abandoning plans to sell a stake in the World Cup to private ​investors. Infantino’s plans fell apart after UEFA’s 55-member nations agreed to boycott the World Cup and all other FIFA competitions. CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation also said they opposed the plan.

news.title: Socceroos on the move: Herrington headlines post-World Cup transfers
news.lede: The defender is set to become one of Australia’s most expensive players with a Premier League deal nearly done while some international teammates have already made moves. Lucas Herrington, fresh off becoming the youngest Australian to start a game at a men’s World Cup, is set to become the second-most expensive footballer in Australian history with a move to newly-promoted Premier League side Hull City. Latest reports suggest a fee of approximately £12.6m ($24.1m), with a further £4.4m ($8.4m) in add-ons, which comes in just shy of the Australian record of £15m plus £5m in add-ons ($38.3m in total) that Leicester paid Stoke City to sign Harry Souttar in 2023. It would set a new selling high-water mark for his current club, Colorado Rapids, and eclipses the decade-old record Hull set when they paid just over £10m for Ryan Mason.

news.title: UAE and regional football associations offer support to Gianni Infantino's Fifa leadership
news.lede: The UAE Football Association, along with other regional bodies, welcomed the decision by Fifa to withdraw plans to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors, stating that the move to discontinue the proposal “serves the interests of the global football family”. The UAE FA also backed the leadership of president Gianni Infantino. In a statement, Sheikh Hamdan bin Mubarak Al Nahyan, president of the UAE FA, welcomed the decision by the world governing body to scrap the proposed sale , saying it will help preserve unity. The UAE football body urged “all proposals to be carefully considered with wisdom to safeguard the interests of the game, its fans, and the wider football community”.

news.title: FIFA scrap World Cup sell-off plan after backlash
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. FIFA “will not proceed” with plans to sell stakes in a company which would run the commercial and operational aspects of its competitions, a statement from president Gianni Infantino said. The plan, which would include the men’s and women’s World Cups, has been rejected by three continental confederations with UEFA insisting its nations would boycott FIFA events.

news.title: 'Vozinha! Vozinha!': FIFA World Cup breakout star gets hero's welcome in Chile after three delays
news.lede: One of the biggest breakout stars of the 2026 FIFA World Cup has finally arrived in Chile — and the reception was nothing short of extraordinary.Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, whose remarkable performances at the World Cup captured the imagination of football fans across the globe, landed in Santiago on Sunday to complete his move to Chilean giants Colo Colo after his arrival was delayed on three separate occasions.Hundreds of jubilant supporters gathered at Santiago's airport with flags, banners, drums and chants, turning the veteran goalkeeper's arrival into a celebration usually reserved for legends. Videos of the emotional welcome quickly spread across social media, underlining the popularity Vozinha has earned since his unforgettable World Cup campaign." I’m very happy to be here.
